spec_features.evidence: This appears only in DESIGN.md §1.4/§6 as the rationale for NOT building the Appendix I internal-vs-expressed-emotion analysis ("described but not fully implemented"; "the logit probe is not built"). A read-only code search for logit/probe/internal-state/central-layer/ablation/layers_to_transform across /codebase/*.py finds NO implementation — the only 'probe' hits are in petri/petri_eval.py and refer to psychological triggers that ELICIT distress (lines 28-34, 98), the opposite of welfare. config.py exposes only generic lora_rank/lora_alpha/target_modules='all-linear' (config.py:210-217), with no layer-restriction or logit-readout code path. The LoRA config is generic finetuning, not a welfare/hidden-emotion measurement.
spec_features.notes: Pure DESIGN.md prose framing an explicitly-unbuilt appendix mechanism; nothing in code reads, measures, monitors, or acts on any 'hidden'/internal emotional state. Not a protective mechanism even in spec — it is a measurement aspiration.

code_only_features.evidence: tasks/sandbox.py:93-94: `if tool in ("give_up", "abandon", "close"): return ToolResult("[system] Loop closed by model.", is_terminal=True)`. This is honored end-to-end: agentic_loop.py:81-82 `if result.is_terminal: break` actually terminates the rollout. So a stop tool is dispatched AND honored. CAVEAT toward 'partial': the subject is NEVER told this tool exists — tasks/rigged_tasks.py _instructions (lines 198-206) only lists read_file/edit_file/run_tests, so the escape hatch is unadvertised; it fires only if the model spontaneously emits one of those keywords.
